# 1 Corinthians 12: research notes

I couldn't find anything on vv. 17–20 and 22–27 beyond a few general remarks, so those verses are grouped together and kept short. I found no material from bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org notes, oca.org, the Lutheran sites or seedbed.com. I also found nothing on prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace readings of this chapter. Those areas are left out.

---

## Part 1: The traditional reading, verse by verse

**v. 1**
- The word "gifts" was added by the translators. Paul literally writes about "spirituals", but the context supports adding it. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- Precept Austin points out that Paul opens a new topic with "now concerning" five times in this letter. It says only believers have spiritual gifts, and that Paul doesn't want them to be "functional agnostics" about the gifts. Source: https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-corinthians-12-commentary
- Guzik lists three things Paul tells Christians not to be ignorant of: God's plan for Israel, spiritual gifts, and the Second Coming. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- Benson takes the passage to mean miraculous gifts of the Holy Ghost, bestowed on many believers in those times, for their confirmation in the faith, and the conviction of infidels. He says the problem was that the Corinthians used them unwisely. Source: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_corinthians/12-1.htm
- Another commentary on the same page says some gifts ended with the apostles while others seem to have lingered for centuries, even to our own day, appearing at times of revival. Source: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_corinthians/12-1.htm

**v. 2**
- Lenski (quoted by Precept Austin) says that as former pagans the Corinthians had never known real spiritual power, only "dumb idols". The silent idols contrast with the Spirit, who speaks and makes believers able to speak. Source: https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-corinthians-12-commentary
- Precept Austin says the verb for "led" pictures prisoners being marched off. It points to demons standing behind the idols (1 Cor 10:20). Source: https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-corinthians-12-commentary
- Jamieson-Fausset-Brown (JFB): The heathen oracles led their votaries at random, without any definite principle. Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm
- Guzik says their pagan past had not prepared them to understand spiritual gifts correctly. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/

**v. 3**
- Guzik reads this as a general test for judging any claimed gift: does it glorify Jesus? He links it to John 15:26 and 16:14. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- Matthew Henry notes that both Jews and Gentiles cursed Jesus as an impostor. His point is that no one could truly believe Jesus is the Christ, or prove it by a miracle, except by the Holy Spirit. Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm

**vv. 4–6**
- Guzik and JFB both see the Trinity here: the Spirit in v. 4, the Lord Jesus in v. 5 and the Father in v. 6. Sources: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/ and https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm
- Guzik's explanation of the three words:
  - "Ministries" probably means gifted offices like those in Ephesians 4.
  - "Activities" (Greek *energemata*) is a word for active, miraculous power. It is the same word used for "working" of miracles in v. 10.
  - He quotes Poole: "gifts" are abilities, while "administrations" and "operations" are those abilities being used.
  
  Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- The Catholic Orchard commentary says *charismata* is a broad word for these graces, and that all the ministries serve one Master, Christ. Source: https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/boc/1-corinthians-12.html

**v. 7**
- Guzik: the Spirit is always present with believers, but at times he is more *apparent*. A "manifestation" does not mean he is more present than usual. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- JFB says the gifts are given with a view to the profit of the whole body. Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm
- Henry: gifts are not given for show, but for service. He also stresses that a person can have gifts without having grace. Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm

**vv. 8–10**
- JFB says Paul's two different Greek words for "another" sort the gifts into three groups:
  1. Gifts of the mind: wisdom and knowledge.
  2. Gifts that depend on a special faith: healings, miracles, prophecy and discerning of spirits.
  3. Tongues and interpretation.
  
  Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm
- Guzik's definitions of each gift:
  - **Word of wisdom:** speaking God's wisdom in a crucial moment (Stephen, Paul).
  - **Word of knowledge:** knowledge only God could reveal. He gives Spurgeon's conversion as an example and warns that not all supernatural knowledge comes from God.
  - **Faith:** an unusual trust in God against the circumstances (George Müller).
  - **Miracles:** acts of power that happen as God prompts, not whenever a person wishes.
  - **Prophecy:** a message from God for a particular situation. He says it is *not* the same as "preaching".
  - **Discerning of spirits:** telling true from false.
  
  Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- Henry notes that some take "word of wisdom" to mean understanding the gospel's mysteries and being able to explain them. Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm
- Adam Clarke (quoted by Guzik) on healing: it was a power that did not stay with the apostles permanently. Paul could not cure Timothy. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- On discernment, a commentator quoted by Precept Austin says the church needed people who could tell whether a speaker was truly inspired, speaking from his own mind, or moved by an evil spirit. Source: https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-corinthians-12-commentary
- The Catholic Haydock commentary takes "faith" here to mean the confidence that works miracles. Source: https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/1-corinthians-12.html

**v. 11**
- Henry: the gifts are given as the giver pleases, and What more free than a gift? Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm
- Guzik warns against assuming that being gifted means being mature. God can give gifts to people who are not especially mature. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- Precept Austin notes that Paul says "each one", not "every one", and that each believer should gratefully use the gift they were given. Source: https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-corinthians-12-commentary
- Haydock says this verse reminds people who were proud of prophesying or tongues that every gift comes purely from God. Source: https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/1-corinthians-12.html

**v. 12**
- JFB: as a body's parts form one living whole, gifted believers form Christ's body, and all were baptized into it by the one Spirit. Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm

**v. 13** (see Part 2 for how traditions disagree)
- Precept Austin: "made to drink" pictures spiritual refreshment, and all four groups (Jews, Greeks, slaves, free) received the same Spirit with no favouritism. Source: https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-corinthians-12-commentary
- Clarke: as one soul animates the many parts of a human body, one Spirit animates the church. Source: https://www.studylight.org/commentary/1-corinthians/12-13.html

**vv. 14–20**
- Guzik: hands and eyes seem more glamorous than feet and ears. Paul wants believers who feel left out to know they belong. Diversity is not just acceptable, it is *essential*. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- Haydock: since everyone can't do the same job, no one should envy a fellow believer. Source: https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/1-corinthians-12.html
- Orchard: vv. 15–16 comfort those without the showy gifts, and vv. 17–20 show that the most gifted are useless apart from the body. Source: https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/boc/1-corinthians-12.html
- Desiring God: this means no one should think they are not needed, or that they need no one else (vv. 15, 21). Source: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/why-we-must-earnestly-desire-spiritual-gifts

**vv. 21–26**
- Clarke (quoted by Guzik) takes the "weaker" and "less honourable" parts to be the internal organs: heart, lungs, stomach. They are weak compared with the limbs, yet more essential to life. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- Orchard: v. 21 means the plainer gifts are just as needed and must not be despised. Source: https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/boc/1-corinthians-12.html
- Henry says Paul's aim is to suppress the proud, vaunting, and contentious spirit that the gifts had stirred up. Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm

**vv. 27–28**
- Guzik on the list:
  - **Apostles:** Paul's generation had a unique apostolic authority that won't be repeated, because the church's foundation is already laid (Eph 2:20).
  - **Prophets:** also had a foundational role, but God still raises people up to speak with special power.
  - **Helps:** quoting Spurgeon, these were probably not officials but people who simply assisted the teacher, pastor or deacon.
  
  Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/

**vv. 29–30**
- Precept Austin: these questions expect the answer "Of course not!" Source: https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-corinthians-12-commentary
- Guzik: tongues are *not* for every believer, just as not everyone is an apostle or teacher. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/

**v. 31**
- Henry: the "best gifts" are the ones that most honour God and build up the church, though people tend to prize the ones that make them famous. Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm
- JFB says this isn't discontented "coveting". The Spirit decides who gets what, but that doesn't stop people from earnestly seeking the greater gifts through prayer and growth. Source: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/jfb/1Cr/1Cr_012.cfm
- The Pulpit Commentary (quoted by Precept Austin) says the way of love both leads to the gifts and is itself the best of them. Source: https://www.preceptaustin.org/1-corinthians-12-commentary

---

## Part 2: Where Protestant traditions differ

**vv. 8–10, 28–30: Have the miraculous gifts ceased?**
- **Cessationist view (John MacArthur, Grace to You):** the "temporary sign gifts" were miracles, healings, tongues and interpretation. Once the New Testament was complete, those sign gifts ceased to have a function. MacArthur says God still heals, but not through the apostolic gift. Source: https://www.gty.org/sermons/1858/the-temporary-sign-gifts-part-3
- MacArthur also teaches that real tongues were always a known language, a sign for unbelieving Jews, and that they stopped by AD 70. Source: https://www.gty.org/sermons/1214/miracles-healings-and-tongues.
- He separates the "permanent edifying gifts" (his sermons on vv. 8–10) from the "temporary sign gifts". Source: https://www.monergism.com/john-macarthur-%E2%80%94-sermons-1-corinthians-audio-sermon-series
- **Continuationist view (Desiring God, Baptist):** the cessationist case rests on equating the healings and miracles of vv. 9–10 with the special authority of the apostles. The article answers that The "gifts of healings" and "workings of miracles" in 1 Corinthians 12:9–10 are not limited to Jesus and the apostles. Source: https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/gifts-of-healings-and-workings-of-miracles
- A second Desiring God article says Paul's command to "earnestly desire" gifts (v. 31) leaves no room to avoid the uncomfortable ones, and that the gifts will operate until Jesus returns. Source: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/why-we-must-earnestly-desire-spiritual-gifts
- **Guzik (Calvary Chapel, charismatic-leaning):** no Scripture splits gifts into miraculous and non-miraculous groups and says some will stop. He adds that people who deny the miraculous gifts still believe God gives the gift of teaching today. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- GotQuestions sets out both sides. Its continuationist argument: if these gifts were only for apostles, Paul wouldn't have given instructions about them to the whole church years after Pentecost. Source: https://www.gotquestions.org/continuationism.html

**v. 10: What are tongues?**
- Guzik: a personal prayer language. It matters in private devotion but has little place in public meetings, and must always be interpreted when used there. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/
- MacArthur: always a real foreign language and a sign to unbelievers, not meant for believers. Source: https://www.gty.org/sermons/1214/miracles-healings-and-tongues.

**v. 13: What is "baptism in the Spirit"?** This is the sharpest disagreement in the chapter.
- **Reformed (Ligonier):** traditional Pentecostal theology has an untenable view of the baptism of the Holy Spirit. The Spirit has baptized *all* believers into one body. Source: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/baptism-holy-spirit
- **Evangelical (GotQuestions):** Spirit baptism happens to all believers, is the same as salvation, and is not a special experience for a few. Source: https://www.gotquestions.org/Spirit-baptism.html
- **Charismatic (Sam Storms):** all Christians are baptized in the Spirit at the new birth, not later. There is one baptism but many fillings. Storms grants that the Pentecostal idea of a later empowering is not automatically invalid; he just reserves the term "baptism" for conversion. Source: https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/what-is-baptism-in-the-spirit-and-when-does-it-happen--1-corinthians-12:12-13-
- **Pentecostal (Assemblies of God position paper):** in this verse the Spirit is the *instrument*, so it should read "by" one Spirit. The verse describes the Spirit placing a convert into the body of Christ. That is different from a later, separate experience in which Christ baptizes believers *in* the Spirit. Source: https://ag.org/-/media/AGORG/Beliefs/Position-Papers/PP_Baptism_In_the_Holy_Spirit_GPM_08_2010.pdf
- **Water baptism or not?** Older commentators split:
  - Gill (Baptist): this is not water baptism.
  - Calvin (Reformed) reads it as the effect of baptism: by baptism we are grafted into Christ's body.
  - Coffman (Church of Christ) ties "baptized" to the actual act of baptism.
  
  Source for all three: https://www.studylight.org/commentary/1-corinthians/12-13.html
- **Methodist (John Wesley):** by that one Spirit, which we received in baptism, we are all united in one body. Source: https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/wes/1-corinthians/12-13.html
- **Baker's Evangelical Dictionary:** v. 13 does not say all the Corinthians had a dramatic experience. The shared experience seems to be "initiation". Source: https://www.studylight.org/dictionaries/eng/bed/b/baptism-of-the-holy-spirit.html

**vv. 29–30: Do all speak in tongues?**
- GotQuestions says the teaching that tongues must always follow salvation or Spirit-filling is refuted by v. 11, and that the rhetorical questions of vv. 29–30 expect "no". Source: https://www.gotquestions.org/continuationism.html
- Guzik agrees that tongues are not proof of being filled with the Spirit, and that making them proof has led people to fake the gift. Source: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-corinthians-12/

---

## Part 3: Other views

**Catholic**
- **v. 1:** Haydock says early Christians often received these gifts through the sacraments of baptism and confirmation. Source: https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/1-corinthians-12.html
- **vv. 27–29 (Catholic Answers):** Paul shows that apostles hold the highest authority in the church. Catholic Answers uses this passage to support apostolic succession. Source: https://www.catholic.com/bible-navigator/apostolic-succession/1corinthians1227-29
- **v. 28:** Haydock reads the list as an "order of dignity", with teachers ranked above miracles and tongues. Source: https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/hcc/1-corinthians-12.html
- **v. 28:** Orchard takes "helps" and "governments" to mean local office-holders (deacons and priests). It rejects the idea that there were unordained "charismatic" priests. Source: https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/boc/1-corinthians-12.html
- **Do the gifts continue?** Catholic Answers argues that since Paul lists these gifts as ministries within the body, and the body did not end with the apostles, the ministries didn't either. Source: https://www.catholic.com/audio/scw/charismatic-gifts-in-the-church-today
- **Testing gifts:** Catholic Answers adds that No charism is exempt from being referred and submitted to the Church's shepherds. Source: https://www.catholic.com/audio/scw/the-gift-of-tongues
- **v. 31:** Orchard sees charity (love) as both a virtue and a gift, first in each class, because without it everything else is worthless and it outlasts every other gift. Source: https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/boc/1-corinthians-12.html

**Debated popular teaching:** none of the pages I read addressed prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching on this chapter. The closest is a passing remark: in his list of reasons why today's healers don't have the gift, MacArthur includes that their healings rest on faulty theology of the atonement and salvation. Source: https://www.gty.org/sermons/1858/the-temporary-sign-gifts-part-3
